newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. military launch harassment inquiry in Germany.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military launch harassment inquiry in Germany.

text.p: U.S. military police have questioned 70 people in an investigation into the alleged sexual harassment of 11 soldiers at a U.S. military training centre in Germany, the U.S. base said on Wednesday.

The Criminal Investigation Command (CID), the U.S. military police, has identified three male suspects who have been relieved of their duties but not yet charged, the 233rd Base Support Batallion said in a statement.
The statement did not specify whether the alleged victims were male or female.
Two of these suspects were apprehended on February 7 and held in pre-trial confinement because a victim alleged they had contacted her in an attempt to influence her testimony.
The third suspect has been ordered not to contact any victim or witness.

The base, in Darmstadt near Frankfurt, said allegations under investigation included rape, forcible sodomy, indecent assault, and cruelty and maltreatment of a subordinate and said a full investigation was being carried out.
Investigations began on February 5, after a female soldier filed an official complaint alleging sexual harassment in December.
